id: title:DanielVisca:charge decompressed bytes on remote write ingestion

observations.code_quote: pub fn decode_write_request(body: &[u8], max_decompressed_bytes: usize) -> Result<WriteRequest> {
observations.behavior: The Prometheus remote-write endpoint's Snappy decoding and protobuf parsing are refactored; this hunk changes the return type of the shared decoder function.
observations.posthog_connection: This change could affect PostHog’s ingestion reliability for users sending metrics via Prometheus Remote Write, since the decoded request and its decompressed byte count become available downstream.

observations.behavior: After successful decoding, the HTTP handler now passes the explicitly computed uncompressed payload size instead of the original compressed body length.
observations.posthog_connection: This could help ensure that quota and rate-limiting counters charge against the actual metric volume rather than the compressed wire size, potentially improving billing or capacity accounting accuracy.

observations.behavior: A new test asserts that the reported uncompressed bytes match the pre-compression input length and also checks that compression actually occurred. This guards against vacuous assertions where no real compression happens.
observations.posthog_connection: These checks support configuration safety and prevent silent misreporting of payload sizes in a path that bypasses the global RequestDecompressionLayer, which is relevant to PostHog's warehouse and managed-warehouse connectors.

The scope is localized to one endpoint and its immediate consumers, without broader systemic restructuring or cross-component dependency changes visible here.
review.posthog_relevance: This could help users relying on Prometheus Remote Write avoid billing or capacity accounting discrepancies caused by charging compressed wire size instead of actual metric volume, especially since the route already bypasses the global request-decompression layer.
